tasks.description: Document collision channels, audit usage, identify redundancies, and establish the foundation for reusable collision presets.
tasks.why_it_matters: Collision configuration affects both gameplay correctness and runtime scalability. High-count persistent collision components can impose substantial hidden cost even when their consuming Blueprint logic is inactive.
acceptance_criteria: For each enemy collision/query component, confirm whether collision needs to be enabled at all.
For each enemy collision/query component, confirm whether overlap events are actually required.
For each enemy collision/query component, confirm which object/channel responses genuinely need to be Block or Overlap rather than Ignore.
For each enemy collision/query component, confirm whether large-radius query components should remain continuously active.
For each enemy collision/query component, evaluate whether explicit or lower-frequency queries would be cheaper than persistent collision volumes.
Benchmark any high-count component whose bounds or collision role suggests significant scaling cost.
Audit Attack_BaseAttackRegion under the EnemyAttackRange preset and establish whether its Static Mesh collision shape has meaningful high-count cost before considering replacement.
context: Enemy collision audit should explicitly include performance impact.
Shooter benchmarking showed that the 3000-unit CannonAimDetectionRadius materially increased UCharacterMovementComponent cost even though its consuming Blueprint logic was disabled.
At 400 Shooters, CharacterMovement measured approximately 7.1 ms with CannonAimDetectionRadius active.
Setting all CannonAimDetectionRadius responses to Ignore reduced CharacterMovement to approximately 4.3 ms in a sampled benchmark frame.
Fully disabling/removing CannonAimDetectionRadius reduced CharacterMovement to approximately 3.7 ms.
Attack_BaseAttackRegion currently uses a Static Mesh as a persistent Detection Volume with the EnemyAttackRange preset.
Do not assume the Static Mesh implementation is expensive; benchmark it before replacing the collision shape.
decisions: Remove the persistent CannonAimDetectionRadius collision component.
CannonAimDetectionRadius existed only to determine whether the current AttackTarget was within aiming range; replace that purpose with a direct distance check.
Removing or fully disabling CannonAimDetectionRadius recovered roughly 4 ms of Game Thread time at 400 Shooters.
Shooter behaviour was validated after CannonAimDetectionRadius removal and continues to work correctly.
Treat large-radius or high-count persistent collision components as potential scaling costs and prefer explicit or lower-frequency queries when they answer the same gameplay question more cheaply.
Benchmark Attack_BaseAttackRegion before making any shape/component replacement.

The dominant scaling concern is therefore the collection of systems running on each enemy rather than simply the number of Actor instances.

tasks.title: Fix enemies failing to retarget walls blocking their path
tasks.description: Fix enemy wall-breaking retargeting so enemies that are physically blocked by player-built walls reliably identify and attack an appropriate blocking wall instead of endlessly continuing movement into the obstruction.
tasks.why_it_matters: Wall-breaking is core to the defensive gameplay loop. If enemies cannot reliably transition from navigation into attacking blocking structures, player-built walls can break enemy behaviour and undermine both combat pressure and the vertical-slice validation of the new lightweight navigation system.
acceptance_criteria: Reproduce the current failure case reliably in a controlled test scenario.

After the blocking wall is destroyed or otherwise ceases to obstruct the route, the enemy resumes navigation toward its normal gameplay target.
Behaviour works with a single wall layer.
Behaviour works with multiple wall layers or successive blocking structures.
Enemies do not incorrectly retarget nearby walls that are not meaningfully blocking their current route.

Avoid redesigning the broader enemy navigation architecture unless the bug investigation demonstrates that a broader change is required.
context: Enemies currently can walk continuously into walls without transitioning into their wall-breaking attack behaviour.

decisions: Treat this as a focused bug fix to the existing wall-breaking/retargeting behaviour rather than a general navigation rewrite.

Resume normal targeting/navigation after the obstruction is removed.
Validate the behaviour against the production lightweight navigation system.
